title: The Human Disease
coreMove: Stop waiting for a mastered life; use Release the Cure Fantasy to trade control fantasies for one imperfect act of work, love, or responsibility now.

exampleSpecs.audience: Sloane, an operations director whose calendar has become a safety project
exampleSpecs.stakes: A useful planning habit is turning into a demand for invulnerability.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Brian Tracy's mastery promise to expose the fantasy that time control can make life safe.

exampleSpecs.audience: Xavier, a graduate who keeps postponing concrete commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: The wish to keep possibility open is preventing any possibility from becoming real.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Connect Marie-Louise von Franz's puer aeternus pattern to job and relationship avoidance.

exampleSpecs.audience: Mederic, a manager exhausted by unsolved human mess
exampleSpecs.stakes: He is treating the existence of recurring problems as proof that he has failed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Charlotte Joko Beck's Zen cure-seeking frame to separate pain from the demand for a cure.

exampleSpecs.audience: Edmund, a parent who expected achievement to feel like arrival
exampleSpecs.stakes: A successful week still contains chores, fatigue, and uncertainty.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Christian Bobin's domestic ordinary moment to show acceptance inside concrete life.

exampleSpecs.audience: Carter, a founder using productivity systems to avoid exposure
exampleSpecs.stakes: The next optimization ritual is delaying a needed honest conversation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show productivity and avoidance sharing the Brian Tracy mastery fantasy.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bruno, a designer afraid that one city will narrow his identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: Avoiding a concrete place is starting to damage work and love.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Marie-Louise von Franz's puer aeternus material to show the cost of refusing time and place.
